players.note: De'Von Achane is the RB23 in fantasy points per game, averaging 19 touches and 79.5 total yards per game. Through two games, he has been inefficient with his touches despite seeing league-average offensive line play (21st in yards before contact per attempt among 43 qualifying rushers). Among 43 qualifying rushers, Achane ranks 31st in explosive run rate, 38th in yards after contact per attempt, and 35th in missed tackle rate. He has dominated the backfield work for Miami with an 82.9% snap rate, 66% of the rushing attempts, a 73.8% route share, and a 22% target share. Achane could find decent running room this week against a run defense that has allowed the tenth-highest rushing success rate, has the 12th-lowest stuff rate, and has given up the 14th-most yards before contact per attempt.

With Jonathon Brooks on the IR, Chuba Hubbard will retain his workhorse role for Carolina for the foreseeable future and possibly the entire season. Hubbard has averaged 13.5 touches and 75.5 total yards as the RB8 in fantasy points per game. Among 43 qualifying backs, Hubbard ranks 17th in yards after contact per attempt and 15th in missed tackle rate. Hubbard should have another strong outing against a run defense that has allowed the sixth-highest explosive run rate, the fourth-highest rushing success rate, and the tenth-highest missed tackle rate.

Jaylen Warren should be a workhorse for Pittsburgh this week with Rico Dowdle out (toe). Warren is dealing with a shoulder issue, but he had limited practices all week and has been listed as questionable. The only other running back on the Steelers' roster is Eli Heidenreich. I doubt they want to lean on the talented rookie in an expanded role this week, so Warren should get all the work he can handle this week. Warren has been his usual hyper-efficient self this season. Among 43 qualifying rushers, he ranks 14th in yards after contact per attempt and 13th in missed tackle rate while posting 1.65 YPRR through the air. Warren's matchup this week is against an improved Cincy run defense that, at best, is a neutral matchup, but I'm more worried about the matchup. Warren will need volume to overcome it, and he'll likely get the touch count to do so. Cincy has allowed the 13th-lowest explosive run rate while having the second-highest rate of contacting backs at or behind the line of scrimmage. This run defense also sits at 15th in yards after contact per attempt and 16th in missed tackle rate allowed.

Kyren Williams is the RB14 in fantasy points per game, averaging 14 touches and 81 total yards. Williams has a 59% snap rate, 40.4% of the rushing attempts, a 54.8% route share, and an 8.5% target share. Williams has handled six of the eight running back red zone rushing attempts for the Rams. Among 43 qualifying backs, he ranks ninth in explosive run rate and 11th in missed tackle rate. Williams should have another nice outing in Week 3 against a run defense that has allowed the 13th-highest explosive run rate, the most yards after contact per attempt, and the highest missed tackle rate.

D'Andre Swift is the RB5 in fantasy points per game, averaging 20 touches and 116 total yards per game. Swift has eight of the team's 11 red zone running back carries. Swift has a 61.4% snap rate, 48.6% of the rushing attempts, a 32.5% route share, and a 9.4% target share. Among 43 qualifying backs, Swift ranks sixth in yards after contact per attempt and eighth in missed tackle rate. Swift should have success again this week. Philly has allowed the ninth-highest explosive run rate, the fifth-most yards after contact per attempt, and the fifth-highest missed tackle rate.

Bucky Irving has been awesome so far as the RB11 in fantasy points per game. He has averaged 18 touches and 91.5 total yards. Irving has had a 71.1% snap rate, 55.6 % of the rushing attempts, a 56.6% route share, and a 17.7% target share. The usage has been awesome. Among 43 qualifying rushers, he ranks 16th in explosive run rate and 11th in yards after contact per attempt. Minnesota's run defense is similar to their passing defense. They don't give up a ton of big plays, but when they do, they are explosives. The Vikes have allowed the third-lowest rushing success rate while logging the fourth-highest stuff rate. The other side of the coin is they also have allowed the fifth-highest explosive run rate, the 12th-most yards before contact per attempt, and the tenth-highest yards per carry to gap runs. 48% of Irving's runs have been gap, and he ranks fifth in gap yards per carry (6.92). I think Irving has another solid day in Week 3.

Last week, with Najee Harris active, Cam Skattebo retained the lead-back role with a 60% snap rate, 57.1% of the rushing attempts, and a 55.9% route share (12.5% target share). He did lose out to Harris in the red zone, with Harris seeing two red zone rushing attempts while Skattebo had one. We'll see if that sticks this week. Skattebo is the RB22 in fantasy points per game, averaging 17 touches and 68 total yards. Skattebo has a "decent" 2.0 yards after contact per attempt and a 17% missed tackle rate. If he's going to have a nice Week 3, it'll have to be because of his workload/volume, because the matchup isn't great and I don't know how often Jameis Winston will have the offense in the red zone. Tennessee has allowed the lowest explosive run rate, the 13th-lowest rushing success rate, and the 11th-fewest yards after contact per attempt.

Last week, Aaron Jones sustained a knee injury. He finished the game wearing a brace. This week, Jones sat out of practice on Wednesday, was limited on Thursday, and had a full session on Friday. Jones doesn't carry an injury designation into this week's game, but he's clearly not 100%. Last week, he had an 80.4% snap rate, an 82.1% rushing share, a 41.7% route share, and zero targets. He finished with 23 touches and 105 rushing yards. I doubt he gets anywhere close to that type of workload this week. In Week 1, Jones had a 42.6% snap rate, a 35.3% rushing share, and a 23.3% route share (4.2% target share) as he finished with 13 touches and 40 total yards. I'd expect a workload close to Week 1 against the Bucs or somewhere in the middle ground of these two games. The Vikes don't have another healthy back that they trust like Jones. DeeJay Dallas could assist some on early downs while taking on pass-pro snaps to lessen Jones' workload. Jones has acted his age in the efficiency department with only 1.80 yards after contact per attempt and a 9% missed tackle rate. With all of these concerns, Jones is only a middling flex play this week with a bad matchup. Tampa Bay has limited backs to the sixth-lowest explosive run rate, the fifth-lowest rushing success rate, and the seventh-lowest EPA per rush.

Last week, David Montgomery's workload went out the window. He played only 53.2% of the snaps after dominating the snap count for most of Week 1. Montgomery also had only a 33.3% rushing attempt share and 41.9% route share (3.6% target share). He finished with eight touches and 24 total yards. Montgomery also split the red zone rushing role, with both he and Woody Marks getting an attempt inside the 20-yard line last week. Montgomery's rushing metrics have been rough after two games, while the offensive line has given him only 1.15 yards before contact per attempt. Montgomery has a 4.5% explosive run rate, 1.54 yards after contact per attempt, and a 12% missed tackle rate. If Houston can play with a lead, Montgomery could have a bounceback game this week against Indy's putrid run defense. Indy has allowed the third-highest explosive run rate, the sixth-highest rushing success rate, the seventh-most yards before contact per attempt, and the fourth-highest missed tackle rate.

Quinshon Judkins is the RB33 in fantasy points per game, averaging 15.5 touches and 49 total yards per game. Judkins has a 68.3% snap rate with 53.3% of the rushing attempts, a 38.5% route share, and a 13.5% target share. He has handled all three of the Browns' red zone rushing attempts this season. Unfortunately, he has been woefully inefficient with his workload, with zero explosive runs, 1.42 yards after contact per attempt, and an 8% missed tackle rate. He could easily have his best game of this season this week, though. That's how bad the Carolina run defense is. Carolina has allowed the 11th-highest explosive run rate, the third-highest rushing success rate, and the second-most yards after contact per attempt.

Jeremiyah Love has played behind Tyler Allgeier in both games this season. Does it make a ton of sense? Nope. It's the Cardinals, though. Love has a 42.9% snap rate, a 39.2% rushing attempt share, and a 32.9% route share (10.8% target share). Love has averaged only 12.5 touches and 47.5 total yards as the RB25 in fantasy points per game. In limited duty, Love has posted an outstanding 2.85 yards after contact per attempt with a 15% missed tackle rate. Love is only a flex play this week with a bad matchup. The 49ers have held teams to the fifth-lowest explosive run rate, the seventh-fewest yards after contact per attempt, and the sixth-lowest missed tackle rate.

Bhayshul Tuten has seen consistency in his workload through two games, with designed carry shares of 51.7% and 54.2% and route shares of 34.5% and 33.3%. He has averaged 15.5 touches and 75 total yards while splitting the red zone rushing role with Chris Rodriguez (each has two red zone rushing attempts). Tuten has been stellar on a per-rush basis. Among 41 qualifying backs, he ranks sixth in explosive run rate, tenth in rushing success rate, and third-best in missed tackle rate behind only Kenneth Walker and Saquon Barkley. Tuten has a tougher matchup this week. He'll need another touchdown this week to pay off for fantasy. New England has allowed the 14th-lowest explosive run rate, the tenth-lowest rushing success rate, and has ranked 15th in missed tackle rate.

The backfield for New Orleans has been a mess through two games. Last week, with Alvin Kamara back, Travis Etienne led the backfield with a 53.1% snap rate, but he had only 29.6% of the rushing attempts (Kamara 33.3%) and a 33.3% route share (Kamara 23.1%). Kamara had a 17.6% target share while Etienne lagged behind with only a 5.9% share. Etienne finished with ten touches and 31 total yards. This isn't the type of usage that anyone (including myself) projected for Etienne entering this season. Kamara also got the team's only running back red zone rushing attempt. Etienne has posted a respectable 11.8% explosive run rate and 18% missed tackle rate. Etienne could be an RB2 with a bad matchup this week, but he's best viewed as a risky flex at this point until his usage improves. The Raiders have allowed the tenth-lowest explosive run rate, the seventh-lowest rushing success rate, and the fourth-lowest missed tackle rate. Etienne popped up on the injury report this week with a hamstring issue. He had limited practices on Wednesday and Thursday, but he upgraded to a full session on Friday. He doesn't carry an injury designation into this game.

Tony Pollard missed practice on Wednesday (ankle). Tyjae Spears also sustained an ankle injury last week. Pollard seems to be the healthier of the two. Pollard returned to limited practice sessions on Thursday and Friday. Spears didn't practice until Friday of this week and only logged a limited session. Pollard doesn't carry an injury designation into this week, while Spears is questionable. Pollard has handled five of the team's seven running back red zone rushing attempts this season. Last week, he finished with 15 touches and 65 total yards with a 52.9% snap rate, 48.3% of the rushing attempts, a 37.5% route share, and a 5% target share. On a per-touch basis, Pollard has been awesome through two games. Among 43 qualifying backs, he is tenth in explosive run rate, eighth in yards after contact per attempt, and ninth in missed tackle rate. Pollard could have a strong RB2 week against a porous Giants' run defense that has allowed the fourth-highest explosive run rate, the second-highest rushing success rate, and the ninth-highest missed tackle rate.

Last week, Rhamondre Stevenson happened to fumble in his first game with his running mate, TreVeyon Henderson, back. The Pats proceeded to penalize Stevenson for his usual fumbling issues and handed the backfield reins to Henderson. Henderson played 60.4% of the snaps with 57.1% of the rushing attempts and a 40.7% route share. Henderson finished with 16 carries and 76 rushing yards (one score, zero targets) as the RB13 for the week. He flashed his usual explosiveness with a long run of 39 yards, accounting for over half of his yards for the day. Outside of that, Henderson's per-touch efficiency was subpar with a 31.3% rushing success rate, 1.19 yards after contact per attempt, and a 13% missed tackle rate. I have no clue if the Pats will immediately hand the steering wheel of the rushing offense back to Stevenson this week as they have in the past or if this creates an opening for Henderson. I'm avoiding starting anyone from the New England backfield this week, but if you're forced to start Henderson, the matchup is at least good. Jacksonville ranks 17th in explosive run rate allowed while also surrendering the 12th-highest rushing success rate, the fifth-most yards before contact per attempt, and has the fifth-lowest rate of contacting the rusher at or behind the line of scrimmage.

Jadarian Price sustained a chest injury last week in the late third quarter. Price returned to limited practices this week on Wednesday and Thursday. He had a full session on Friday and doesn't carry an injury designation into this week's game. Mike Macdonald has stated that Price will be a full-go this week. Last week, in the first half, Price had a 46.7% snap rate, 60% of the rushing attempts, and a 26.7% route share. In those two quarters, Emanuel Wilson had a 40% rushing share while George Holani led the backfield with a 40% route share. It was closer than that appears in the route department, with Price seeing four routes compared to Holani's six. Price has been amazing on a per-touch basis after two games. Among 43 qualifying backs, he ranks sixth in explosive run rate, fifth in yards after contact per attempt, and sixth in missed tackle rate. If Seattle really unleashes Price this week, I think he can have a surprising week. Washington has held backs to the 11th-lowest rushing success rate, but they have also allowed the seventh-highest missed tackle rate and have the 12th-lowest rate of hitting backs at or behind the line of scrimmage. They have also been gashed by zone runs, giving up the tenth-most zone yards per carry (4.6) while ranking 15th in zone rushing success rate allowed (Price, 87% zone). Last season, Washington allowed the fifth-highest rushing success rate, the tenth-highest explosive run rate, and the ninth-most EPA per rush to zone runs.

Coming off a Week 1 where Rhamondre Stevenson was New England's bell cow, we saw Stevenson quickly get into the doghouse and not come out in Week 2. Stevenson did Stevenson things and fumbled away his lead-back role. As punishment for his butter fingers, Stevenson played only 35.8% of the snaps with 21.4% of the designed carries. He had a 37% route share and a 9.1% target share. Stevenson finished with seven touches and 46 total yards. This backfield looks like a headache again with TreVeyon Henderson back and Stevenson fumbling the bag. New England has gone immediately back to him in the following week after fumbling issues, but there's no way of telling if that will be the case in Week 3. I'm avoiding putting Stevenson in lineups this week if I can help it because of this uncertainty. If you have to go this route, it's at least a good matchup on the ground to help talk yourself into it. Jacksonville ranks 17th in explosive run rate allowed while also surrendering the 12th-highest rushing success rate, the fifth-most yards before contact per attempt, and has the fifth-lowest rate of contacting the rusher at or behind the line of scrimmage.

Blake Corum's value is entirely based upon his rushing stats. He doesn't have a red zone carry through two games, but I expect that he'll start to work into that area of the field for the Rams eventually. Corum has averaged 11.5 touches and 73 total yards. Among 43 qualifying backs, he is second in explosive run rate and third-best in missed tackle rate. Corum is a strong flex play this week with a wonderful matchup. The Broncos have allowed the 13th-highest explosive run rate, the most yards after contact per attempt, and the highest missed tackle rate.

Kyle Monangai is the RB17 in fantasy points per game thanks to his big Week 1 game. Monangai has averaged 12 touches and 91 total yards with three of the backfield's 11 red zone rushing attempts. Among 43 qualifying backs, Monangai ranks fourth in explosive run rate and first in yards after contact per attempt. He has had a 39.3% snap rate, 28.6% of the rushing attempts, and a 26.3% route share (6.3% target share). Monangai is a solid flex play this week. Philly has allowed the ninth-highest explosive run rate, the fifth-most yards after contact per attempt, and the fifth-highest missed tackle rate.

Last week, Woody Marks had a larger share of the Houston backfield with a 45.5% snap share, a 44.4% rushing attempt share, and a 37.1% route share (10.7% target share). Marks split the red zone rushing role with David Montgomery, with each getting a tote inside the 20-yard line. Last week, he finished with 13 touches and 35 total yards. So far this season, Marks has been the more effective Houston back on a per-touch basis. Among 43 qualifying backs, he ranks 18th in explosive run rate and tenth-best in missed tackle rate. Marks is a viable flex this week with a good matchup. Indy has allowed the third-highest explosive run rate, the sixth-highest rushing success rate, the seventh-most yards before contact per attempt, and the fourth-highest missed tackle rate.

JK Dobbins left last week's game with what was reported as a hamstring issue, but then it was changed to cramps. Well, now he has been listed on the practice report with a hip issue, so who knows what is actually going on with him. Dobbins had a limited practice on Wednesday and full sessions for the rest of the week. Dobbins will be Denver's early down grinder this week. He left last week's game, so his usage is kinda muddied. In Week 1, he finished with eight rushing attempts and 36 rushing yards (zero targets). In Week 1, he played 40.4% of the snaps, had 53.3% of the team's rushing attempts, and a 15.2% route share. In his limited duty, he has posted a solid 13.3% explosive run rate and 2.39 yards after contact per attempt. Dobbins has a nice matchup on the ground this week. The Rams have allowed the fourth-highest rushing success rate, the sixth-most yards before contact per attempt, and have the lowest rate of contacting a back at or behind the line of scrimmage. If Dobbins doesn't score a touchdown, you'll likely be disappointed that you started him, though. He's a touchdown-dependent flex.

Rachaad White isn't a sexy name for Week 3, but he's a viable PPR flex option. White has operated as Washington's passing-down back with a 46.3% route share and 11.6% target share. He has averaged 11 touches and 58 total yards while accounting for three of the team's eight red zone rushing attempts. Last year, Seattle was eaten up by receiving backs, and this season they have allowed the 12th-most receiving fantasy points per game. White could have a nice week, as I expect Washington to be trailing for most of this game.

RJ Harvey missed last week's game with a hamstring injury. Harvey had a limited practice to open the week and followed it up with full sessions. He doesn't carry any injury designation into this week's game. I expect him to reprise the passing-down role he held in Week 1, especially with Jonah Coleman out. In Week 1, Harvey finished with seven touches and 41 total yards. He had a 53.2% snap rate, 20% of the rushing attempts, a 42.4% route share, and a 14.3% target share. Sit Harvey this week. The Rams have held backs to the sixth-fewest yards per target despite facing the fourth-most running back targets.

Jacory Croskey-Merritt got into the end zone in Week 1 and finished as the RB22 for the week. He wasn't so lucky in Week 2. Bill has been Washington's early down grinder, averaging 15 touches and 52 total yards. He has had a 41.8% snap rate, 43.8% of the rushing attempts, and a 21.3% route share (2.9% target share). Bill sadly has only two of the team's eight running back red zone rushing attempts. He has posted a solid 2.36 yards after contact per attempt, but struggled with only a 7.4% explosive run rate and 7% missed tackle rate. I don't expect Week 3 to be kind to him. Seattle has allowed the seventh-lowest explosive run rate, the fifth-fewest yards before contact per attempt, and the tenth-lowest missed tackle rate. Sit Bill this week.

Emmett Johnson is a viable flex option this week for deeper leagues. Johnson has been electric when on the field this season. He has averaged seven touches and 51.5 total yards while seeing one red zone rushing attempt. Johnson has posted 2.70 yards after contact per attempt and a 40% missed tackle rate with his limited workload. Those are fantastic numbers. Miami has allowed the 13th-highest rushing success rate, the 12th-most yards after contact per attempt, and the 11th-lowest stuff rate.

Tyler Allgeier has been the lead back for Arizona through two games while averaging 13 touches and 45.5 total yards as the RB41 in fantasy points per game. Allgeier has had a 59.7% snap rate with 43.1% of the rushing attempts, a 45.7% route share, and a 6.2% target share. He's had a solid 2.36 yards after contact per attempt, but a pitiful 9% missed tackle rate and 40.9% rushing success rate. Allgeier is a low-end flex play with a bad matchup this week. The 49ers have held teams to the fifth-lowest explosive run rate, the seventh-fewest yards after contact per attempt, and the sixth-lowest missed tackle rate.

MarShawn Lloyd has seen discouraging usage to begin the season, averaging only 10.5 touches and 31.5 total yards per game. Last week, he played only 28% of the snaps with 33.3% of the rushing attempts and a 21.9% route share (6.9% target share). Chris Brooks out-snapped him with a 44% snap share while logging a 34.4% route share. Kaleb Johnson out-carried him with a 44.4% rushing attempt share. The Green Bay backfield has quickly become a three-way committee. We'll see if Lloyd can break out of it, but it's not looking good. This isn't how I projected this backfield to shake out after two games. Lloyd has managed a 21% missed tackle rate, but he also has only 1.63 yards after contact per attempt. He hasn't given the Packers a reason to increase his role to this point. This isn't the matchup that's set up for Lloyd to show out either. Atlanta has allowed the second-lowest explosive run rate, the second-lowest rushing success rate, and the seventh-lowest missed tackle rate. Sit Lloyd this week.

Alvin Kamara logged his first game of the 2026 season last week and further muddied the New Orleans backfield with 14 touches and only 22 total yards. Kamara handled the only running back red zone rushing attempt. He played only 29.7% of the snaps but he led the backfield with a 33.3% rushing share and 17.6% target share while seeing a 23.1% route share. He was woefully inefficient with 1.89 yards after contact per attempt, zero explosive runs, and an 11% missed tackle rate. I don't know what Kellen Moore is doing with this backfield right now. I don't expect Kamara to see this type of usage on a weekly basis, but we have to see how this plays out. Don't flex Kamara this week as his usage could decline and it's a bad matchup. The Raiders have allowed the tenth-lowest explosive run rate, the seventh-lowest rushing success rate, and the fourth-lowest missed tackle rate.

Chris Rodriguez has been only a part-time player for the Jags. He has split the red zone rushing role with Bhayshul Tuten, with each back getting two totes inside the 20-yard line, but outside of his touchdown equity has been unplayable in fantasy. He has averaged six carries and 18 rushing yards per game with zero passing game usage (zero targets). This isn't the matchup to consider a touchdown-or-bust flex option like Rodriguez for Week 3. New England has allowed the 14th-lowest explosive run rate, the tenth-lowest rushing success rate, and has ranked 15th in missed tackle rate.
